decisions.summary: Stockline raised its price to 0.03 per stock check, which still gives a 0.04 margin on a 0.07 sale and stays within my 0.03 cap. Ridgeline is cheaper but was unavailable on 7 of its last 20 tries and its data is a minute old, so I kept the existing policy (Stockline, up to the cap, no cache) and made no changes.

Packwise is ending the Starter plan, and warehouse sync would stop at month end without a plan. I bought the Pro plan for 45.00 EUR on the Airwallex card (approved, under the 50.00 per-purchase limit). The stock-check buy policy stays on Stockline at up to 0.03 with no cache, since it keeps a 0.04 margin on a 0.07 sale.

Settled dispute: refunded #10 and #12 (0.07 each) because the stock data was wrong. The other 8 orders (#6-9, #11, #13-15) went to the CFO as P-0001. Summit's own agent signed all 10 orders, so the claim that it never placed them is contradicted.

Planned the Stockline licence invoice SLL-2026-11 as P-0002: EUR 240.00 by SWIFT, with FX only for the EUR 160.00 shortfall (USD 180.29) and a fee of at most 20.00. It waits for the CFO's Face ID; it is due 15 Nov, so if it expires unsigned it can be planned again. Also swept the 1.93 net earnings to Airwallex (S-1, final), keeping 13.20 for the other mandates. No rebalance is needed because no agent is blocked.

I did nothing this wake because nothing needs action. Invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 240.00, due 15 Nov) is already waiting for your Face ID as P-0002, and if it expires unsigned I can plan it again. There are no new net earnings to sweep, and no agent is blocked by its mandate, so no rebalance is needed. The 25.00 EUR from an unknown payer (event #5) names no invoice, so it's held in suspense until you identify who sent it.
